Objective: Check nitrate exposure before prescribing a PDE5 inhibitor
ChangedEvidence: A patient without a contraindication changes to one using rescue nitroglycerin.

Objective: Separate association, confounding and individual causation in cannabis fertility studies
ChangedEvidence: A crude exposure comparison changes to a comparison in which tobacco exposure is balanced.

Objective: Interpret semen results in a cannabis user without assuming causality
ChangedEvidence: Confirmed azoospermia changes to a single low-volume sample known to be incomplete.

Objective: Counsel about cannabis exposure and fertility without promising a treatment effect
ChangedEvidence: A request for a guarantee after cessation changes to a question about interpreting spontaneous conception during continued use.

Objective: Identify medications that make sildenafil unsafe through additive cGMP signaling
ChangedEvidence: A guanylate cyclase stimulator changes to an intermittently used nitrate omitted from the scheduled medication list.

Objective: Communicate recent PDE5 exposure when acute chest pain is assessed
ChangedEvidence: Prescribing safety before exposure changes to emergency medication reconciliation after a dose.

Objective: Localize retroareolar tissue and an eccentric mass by ultrasound
ChangedEvidence: A retroareolar disk is compared with an eccentric solid mass outside the nipple-areolar complex.

Objective: Distinguish a suspicious eccentric mass from a central glandular pattern on mammography
ChangedEvidence: A fan-shaped central opacity changes to a discrete eccentric high-density lesion on a different mammogram.

Objective: Interpret renin and aldosterone responses to dietary sodium
ChangedEvidence: Restriction is assessed from renin activity in one case. The other asks for the sodium exposure consistent with a lower aldosterone level.

Objective: Compare actual sodium exposure at a specified meal portion
ChangedEvidence: Different units and a different serving-size ratio reverse which label supplies less sodium at the chosen portion.

Objective: Choose a salt replacement in light of potassium excretion
ChangedEvidence: Renal potassium handling changes from intact to impaired with recurrent hyperkalemia.

Objective: Use the composition of urinary protein to localize the dominant renal defect
ChangedEvidence: Predominantly low-molecular-weight proteins change to albumin-dominant proteinuria with a glomerular sediment.

Objective: Use fractional phosphate excretion to distinguish renal wasting from an appropriate renal response
ChangedEvidence: Inappropriately high fractional excretion while phosphate is low changes to marked renal conservation after poor intake.

Objective: Preserve hepatitis B suppression while changing therapy for proximal tubulopathy
ChangedEvidence: HBV status must first be established in one patient. Confirmed chronic HBV and inability to use either tenofovir formulation determine the alternative in another.

Objective: Read preserved effort when upper-airway flow falls
ChangedEvidence: The second patient has a different belt location, smaller efforts and an interval of recovery before the shaded segment.

Objective: Predict loss of drive from the carbon dioxide reserve in non-REM sleep
ChangedEvidence: The second sleeper has a larger reserve. The same fall in carbon dioxide now leaves the level above the measured threshold.

Objective: Choose the denominator for a respiratory event index
ChangedEvidence: An attended study measures sleep time in the first patient. A different home study provides only valid monitoring time.

Objective: Distinguish absent inspiratory effort from incomplete or mixed evidence
ChangedEvidence: Absent effort throughout a scored apnea changes to unequivocal return of effort before flow resumes. Two other patients illustrate the limits of a single belt.

Objective: Use objective PAP downloads to choose the next troubleshooting step
ChangedEvidence: Short nightly use with low leak changes to full-night use with an obvious interface leak.

Objective: Evaluate whether a bilevel mode can deliver breaths during absent drive
ChangedEvidence: Choosing a bilevel mode after specialist assessment changes to identifying why a running spontaneous-only device fails during a central pause.

Objective: Balance the essential substrate against its impaired conversion in neonatal dietary treatment
ChangedEvidence: A growing infant with repeatedly low phenylalanine needs reassessment of substrate intake. Low tyrosine despite in-range phenylalanine changes the nutrient under review.

Objective: Separate confirmatory sampling from specialist-directed dietary treatment
ChangedEvidence: An abnormal screening result changes to confirmed persistent PAH deficiency above the treatment threshold.

Objective: Investigate a rising phenylalanine concentration using intake and energy balance
ChangedEvidence: Febrile illness with inadequate energy changes to a thriving infant whose measured intact-protein intake has increased.

Objective: Predict which digestive defect pancreatic replacement can correct
ChangedEvidence: Pancreatic enzyme deficiency changes to impaired bile delivery despite normal pancreatic enzymes.

Objective: Use pancreatic function and growth to interpret feeding symptoms in cystic fibrosis
ChangedEvidence: An infant has overt malabsorption with low fecal elastase. A different infant with a sufficient result has normal stools but an inadequate measured intake.

Objective: Locate gaps in pancreatic enzyme delivery before changing a prescription
ChangedEvidence: Missed snack doses change to dosing every eating occasion but taking capsules well after meals.

Objective: Identify what a nutrition referral must investigate in treated celiac disease
ChangedEvidence: A hidden gluten exposure in a barley ingredient changes to a diet meeting gluten restrictions but providing few iron sources.

Objective: Distinguish dietary causes of symptoms after a celiac diagnosis
ChangedEvidence: Evidence of gluten cross-contact changes to dose-dependent symptoms confined to lactose despite verified gluten avoidance.

Objective: Choose the next evaluation when symptoms persist on a gluten-free diet
ChangedEvidence: Documented cross-contact changes to persistent weight loss after a specialist dietitian confirms adherence and exposure sources are addressed.

Objective: Distinguish the substrate for lactase treatment from milk-protein reactions
ChangedEvidence: A dose-related intestinal response changes to an immediate systemic reaction despite using lactose-free cow’s milk.

Objective: Choose a targeted evaluation using timing and organ involvement after milk exposure
ChangedEvidence: Delayed isolated gastrointestinal symptoms change to a history of rapid urticaria and wheeze after a small amount of milk.

Objective: Preserve dietary calcium while adapting dairy choices to tolerance
ChangedEvidence: One patient prefers lactose-free cow’s milk. Another wants no dairy and must compare two alternatives for fortification.

Objective: Recognize language and numeracy barriers when explaining a feeding plan
ChangedEvidence: A language mismatch changes to confusion about serving units despite use of the preferred language.

Objective: Adapt the way dietary instructions are communicated to the demonstrated barrier
ChangedEvidence: A qualified interpreter is needed for spoken instructions in one case. Low reading proficiency in the preferred language changes the needed format in another.

Objective: Correct a feeding-plan misunderstanding at handoff
ChangedEvidence: Correct interpretation but a measuring error changes to correct demonstration with a new caregiver who has never received the instructions.

Objective: Use hemodynamic findings to decide whether an effusion explains shock
ChangedEvidence: An incidental effusion during sepsis changes to a new effusion with impaired filling and shock.

Objective: Choose management from the involved vessel and the bowel examination
ChangedEvidence: A stable venous thrombosis with intact bowel changes to generalized peritonitis despite anticoagulation.

Objective: Interpret a positive ascites culture when the first cell count is low
ChangedEvidence: The initial asymptomatic low-count culture changes either to cleared fluid or a neutrophil rise above the treatment threshold.

Objective: Choose the care setting after initial treatment of chemotherapy-associated febrile neutropenia
ChangedEvidence: Two stable patients have similar clinical risks but differ in their ability to reach urgent care and maintain follow-up.

Objective: Choose follow-up parasitemia testing from symptoms and immune status
ChangedEvidence: Resolved symptoms in an immunocompetent adult change to clinical improvement after B-cell depletion, which carries a higher relapse risk.

Objective: Calculate the effective distending pressure of a cardiac chamber
ChangedEvidence: External pressure rises while chamber pressure stays fixed; in a second measurement both pressures rise equally.

Objective: Measure inspiratory systolic pressure change in suspected tamponade
ChangedEvidence: Marked variation during spontaneous breathing changes to a small respiratory fluctuation.

Objective: Distinguish pressure loss at arterial inflow from high venous outflow pressure
ChangedEvidence: Arterial pressure falls in one bowel segment; the other has normal arterial pressure but elevated venous pressure.

Objective: Distinguish arterial and venous occlusion on contrast imaging
ChangedEvidence: A superior mesenteric arterial filling defect changes to a venous filling defect with venous congestion.

Objective: Distinguish change in a cell percentage from change in the absolute ascitic neutrophil count
ChangedEvidence: A declining percentage accompanies a rising absolute count in one pair; the reverse occurs in the other.

Objective: Distinguish asymptomatic bacterascites from symptomatic low-count infection
ChangedEvidence: A well patient with a low-count positive culture changes to a patient with fever and abdominal pain while cell counts are still low.

Objective: Interpret local inflammatory findings when granulocyte recruitment is impaired
ChangedEvidence: A deceptively bland wound during profound neutropenia changes to visible exudate as neutrophils recover.

Objective: Assess infection risk when fever or the current ANC is misleading
ChangedEvidence: A count above 500 with an imminent decline changes to profound neutropenia with shock but little fever.

Objective: Interpret the marrow response to red-cell destruction
ChangedEvidence: Compensatory reticulocytosis changes to an inappropriately low reticulocyte response during marrow suppression.

Objective: Decide when additional testing is needed despite a first negative result
ChangedEvidence: A single negative smear in a symptomatic exposed patient changes to persistent antibody after a remote, resolved illness.

Objective: Does suspected pneumothorax need decompression before diagnostic imaging?
ChangedEvidence: Shock and severe respiratory compromise change to a hemodynamically stable patient without severe compromise.

Objective: Does persistent pain on disease-modifying treatment show ongoing inflammation?
ChangedEvidence: Objective synovitis despite optimized therapy changes to localized use-related pain with the inflammatory disease at target.

Objective: Does the location of the aortic tear require immediate operative repair?
ChangedEvidence: Ascending involvement changes to an uncomplicated descending dissection without rupture or malperfusion.

Objective: Can the patient leave acute care after initial bronchodilator treatment?
ChangedEvidence: Sustained clinical recovery with reliable home care changes to drowsiness and worsening airflow despite initial treatment.

Objective: Which problem requires the next intervention as ketoacidosis and sepsis evolve?
ChangedEvidence: A resolved metabolic crisis with persistent septic shock changes to normalized glucose with ongoing ketosis in a stable patient.

Objective: Do recurrent symptoms call for additional seizure treatment or management of magnesium toxicity?
ChangedEvidence: A recurrent eclamptic seizure with intact reflexes and ventilation changes to hyporeflexia and hypoventilation during magnesium infusion.

Objective: Track ketone production and the limitations of a urine ketone strip
ChangedEvidence: Low urine ketones early in illness and rising strip intensity during recovery reflect different proportions of the circulating ketones.

Objective: Detect ketoacidosis with modest hyperglycemia and distinguish isolated ketosis
ChangedEvidence: A second presentation has ketonemia during fasting but lacks the metabolic acidosis required for DKA.

Objective: Maintain insulin coverage as glucose falls and during transition off intravenous insulin
ChangedEvidence: The first case still needs insulin to suppress ketogenesis; the second has resolved DKA and needs overlap to prevent rebound.

Objective: Explain profound dehydration with little ketonemia in HHS
ChangedEvidence: One case tests residual anti-lipolytic insulin activity; the other tests volume loss despite marked glycosuria.

Objective: Recognize hypovolemia and adapt initial fluid delivery to cardiac reserve
ChangedEvidence: Shock in an adult with preserved cardiac reserve and congestion risk in an elderly adult require different fluid delivery strategies.

Objective: Assess recovery from HHS beyond the blood glucose value
ChangedEvidence: Persistent hyperosmolality and oliguria prevent declaring recovery in one case, while persistent confusion after biochemical recovery needs another explanation.

Objective: Explain changes in measured sodium as extracellular glucose changes
ChangedEvidence: The first case tracks water moving outward during hyperglycemia and the second tracks water returning during treatment.

Objective: Decide when phosphate depletion in DKA warrants replacement
ChangedEvidence: An asymptomatic moderate decrease gives way to severe depletion accompanied by respiratory muscle weakness.

Objective: Distinguish an expected sodium rise from failure of osmolality to fall
ChangedEvidence: A falling osmolality supports the current trajectory, while persistent hyperosmolality despite adequate balance and insulin changes the fluid decision.

Objective: Distinguish autonomic warning symptoms from neuroglycopenia
ChangedEvidence: One patient retains an early sympathetic warning; another first shows impaired cognition after repeated lows.

Objective: Identify a severe event despite missing or misleading glucose measurements
ChangedEvidence: A rescued episode lacks a pretreatment glucose, while a much lower measured value is treated independently.

Objective: Equip household members to rescue a patient who cannot take oral glucose
ChangedEvidence: The rescue plan changes from advance training to an immediate out-of-hospital glucagon decision.

Objective: Trace metabolic fuel mobilization when basal insulin is absent
ChangedEvidence: The fasting liver releases more glucose in one case, while adipose tissue supplies fatty acids for ketone production in the other.

Objective: Recognize clinical diabetes and determine when confirmation is required
ChangedEvidence: Classic symptoms and random hyperglycemia establish diabetes immediately, while an asymptomatic incidental value requires confirmation.

Objective: Prevent insulin interruption when inpatient pump use becomes unsafe
ChangedEvidence: Competent self-management with institutional support permits pump use, while loss of capacity requires scheduled coverage without a basal gap.

Objective: Interpret compensatory insulin secretion during insulin resistance
ChangedEvidence: An early meal response shows compensation; a later state shows inadequate secretion despite persistent resistance.

Objective: Select a valid confirmatory diagnostic test when A1C and glucose disagree
ChangedEvidence: Interference from recent transfusion calls for plasma glucose; an otherwise valid discordant result calls for repeating the abnormal test.

Objective: Choose glucose-lowering therapy for cardiorenal benefit at an already adequate A1C
ChangedEvidence: Established heart failure prioritizes an SGLT2 inhibitor, while severe gastroparesis changes the suitability of a GLP-1–based option.

Objective: Distinguish retinal vascular leakage from the angiogenic response to ischemia
ChangedEvidence: Hard exudates in one clinical photograph reflect leakage; new surface vessels in the other reflect ischemia-driven angiogenesis.

Objective: Localize two causes of decreased vision in diabetic eye disease
ChangedEvidence: Gradual loss of central detail with intraretinal fluid localizes to the macula, whereas abrupt floaters and a hazy fundus suggest blood in the vitreous.

Objective: Choose eye treatment according to the lesion and ability to return for follow-up
ChangedEvidence: Center-involving edema with impaired vision favors intravitreal treatment, while unreliable follow-up changes the discussion of therapy for proliferative disease.

Objective: Relate sensory fiber type to modalities lost in diabetic polyneuropathy
ChangedEvidence: Pain and temperature loss implicate small fibers, whereas loss of vibration and position sense points to large fibers.

Objective: Identify atypical neuropathy that warrants investigating an additional cause
ChangedEvidence: A typical chronic length-dependent sensory pattern differs from rapid unilateral motor onset.

Objective: Protect an insensate foot when inflammatory signs suggest acute Charcot disease
ChangedEvidence: New unilateral warmth requires immediate offloading, while a normal early radiograph does not justify resuming weight bearing.

Objective: Explain why albuminuria and filtration are complementary measurements
ChangedEvidence: One kidney shows increased albumin passage with preserved filtration; another has a persistently low eGFR despite little albuminuria.

Objective: Identify findings that suggest an additional renal diagnosis in diabetes
ChangedEvidence: A slowly evolving albuminuric course differs from an abrupt nephritic presentation.

Objective: Interpret the initial creatinine response to renin–angiotensin system blockade
ChangedEvidence: A modest stable rise in a euvolemic patient differs from a larger rise with volume depletion.

Objective: Trace renal salt loss and compensatory renin release in adrenal cortical failure
ChangedEvidence: Renin rises with untreated salt loss but falls with excessive mineralocorticoid effect.

Objective: Determine the cause of confirmed primary adrenal insufficiency
ChangedEvidence: Autoantibody positivity supports autoimmune disease, while negative antibodies plus bilateral enlargement redirect the etiologic evaluation.

Objective: Use symptoms, standing pressure and electrolytes to monitor fludrocortisone
ChangedEvidence: Persistent salt craving and orthostasis suggest insufficient mineralocorticoid effect, whereas new hypertension prompts dose reassessment.

Objective: Explain dilutional hyponatremia with preserved mineralocorticoid activity
ChangedEvidence: Concentrated urine in cortisol deficiency reflects impaired free-water clearance; marked hyperkalemia points to an additional process.

Objective: Select and interpret morning cortisol testing in stable patients with pituitary disease
ChangedEvidence: A clearly low morning value supports central adrenal failure, while an intermediate value requires stimulation testing.

Objective: Sequence adrenal and thyroid replacement in pituitary disease
ChangedEvidence: A confirmed deficiency needs glucocorticoid first; when testing must be deferred, empiric coverage permits urgent thyroid replacement.

Objective: Predict ACTH and contralateral adrenal changes in autonomous cortisol secretion
ChangedEvidence: A unilateral cortisol-secreting tumor suppresses the opposite cortex, while excess ACTH drives both glands.

Objective: Recognize misleading cortisol screening results from altered binding or filtration
ChangedEvidence: Oral estrogen changes total serum cortisol; severe renal failure reduces the usefulness of urinary free cortisol.

Objective: Manage postoperative hypocortisolism after successful removal of a cortisol source
ChangedEvidence: Immediate biochemical deficiency requires replacement; later discontinuation depends on evidence of axis recovery.

Objective: Connect mineralocorticoid action to paired potassium and acid–base findings
ChangedEvidence: One sample illustrates renal potassium wasting, while the second traces alkalosis to enhanced distal hydrogen secretion.

Objective: Identify false-negative and false-positive aldosteronism screens
ChangedEvidence: Low potassium can suppress aldosterone whereas beta-blocker therapy can suppress renin and raise the ratio.

Objective: Monitor medical therapy for autonomous aldosterone secretion
ChangedEvidence: Baseline potassium depletion can correct with blockade; new hyperkalemia and renal dysfunction change the plan.

Objective: Separate the tissue property measured on CT from adrenal secretory function
ChangedEvidence: Two lipid-rich nodules look equally benign on CT but suppress cortisol differently.

Objective: Select hormonal evaluation from the clinical context of an incidental adrenal mass
ChangedEvidence: Hypertension with hypokalemia prioritizes aldosterone–renin testing; an indeterminate adrenal lesion with adrenergic spells needs catecholamine-metabolite testing.

Objective: Decide when biopsy of an indeterminate adrenal lesion could change care
ChangedEvidence: A cancer staging decision may justify biopsy after hormonal evaluation, whereas unequivocal benign imaging removes the indication.

Objective: Explain arterial noncompressibility and its effect on ankle pressure measurements
ChangedEvidence: One tracing shows an artifactually high ankle pressure; a distal measurement detects impaired perfusion in the same clinical setting.

Objective: Select physiologic testing for suspected PAD when resting ABI is inconclusive
ChangedEvidence: A noncompressible ABI calls for a toe measurement; exertional symptoms with a normal compressible ABI call for exercise testing.

Objective: Distinguish stable claudication from threatened limb perfusion
ChangedEvidence: Stable exertional symptoms permit structured exercise, whereas persistent rest pain and tissue loss require prompt limb-salvage evaluation.

Objective: Trace mismatch between insulin action and delayed nutrient absorption
ChangedEvidence: The first tracing shows rapid insulin action before carbohydrate appearance; the second shows late hyperglycemia as absorption catches up.

Objective: Identify reversible influences before interpreting a gastric-emptying result
ChangedEvidence: A motility-slowing drug and acute hyperglycemia each alter how delayed emptying should be interpreted.

Objective: Escalate nutritional support according to oral tolerance in gastroparesis
ChangedEvidence: Maintained oral intake supports dietary adaptation; ongoing malnutrition despite that strategy warrants postpyloric support.

Objective: Decide when diagnostic sampling can precede rescue steroids and when further shock evaluation is needed
ChangedEvidence: Before treatment a blood draw is possible without delay. Persistent shock after initial treatment needs parallel evaluation for a precipitant.

Objective: Determine whether a spontaneous episode can supply a diagnostic critical sample
ChangedEvidence: A simultaneous sample is feasible during a stable spontaneous low; absent a pre-rescue sample, a later supervised evaluation may be necessary.

Objective: Convert kidney trial event proportions into absolute risk differences and NNT
ChangedEvidence: Observed DAPA-CKD event rates and a lower-risk hypothetical population illustrate how baseline risk changes absolute benefit.

Objective: Assess applicability and component-level claims from DAPA-CKD
ChangedEvidence: One question compares a patient with the enrollment range. A separate question asks which individual endpoint can be inferred from a composite result.

Objective: Separate the visual-cycle and epithelial functions of vitamin A
ChangedEvidence: Delayed dark adaptation points to retinal pigment function, whereas a conjunctival lesion points to epithelial differentiation.

Objective: Identify an ocular presentation that requires prompt assessment for vitamin A deficiency
ChangedEvidence: Dry conjunctival plaques and night blindness suggest xerophthalmia; isolated lens opacity localizes visual loss elsewhere.

Objective: Distinguish correcting poor intake from addressing ongoing fat malabsorption
ChangedEvidence: Low supply with normal absorption permits a dietary plan, whereas ongoing cholestasis despite intake requires assessment of impaired absorption.

Objective: Link niacin availability to redox coenzymes and energy metabolism
ChangedEvidence: One reaction reduces NAD⁺ during substrate oxidation; a biosynthetic reaction uses reducing power from NADPH.

Objective: Recognize the distribution of pellagrous dermatitis on different skin sites
ChangedEvidence: The first photograph shows bilateral dorsal hand involvement; the second shows the characteristic exposed neckline.

Objective: Distinguish inadequate niacin equivalents from diversion of a precursor
ChangedEvidence: A monotonous low-protein diet reduces available niacin equivalents, while persistent pellagra despite food access can signal altered tryptophan handling.

Objective: Trace defective thymidylate synthesis to megaloblastic maturation
ChangedEvidence: A marrow precursor shows impaired nuclear maturation; an anemia dominated by iron-limited hemoglobin production has a different cell-size pattern.

Objective: Evaluate macrocytosis while accounting for coexisting deficiencies
ChangedEvidence: Averages can mask mixed microcytic and macrocytic populations; a separate presentation with neurologic signs requires evaluation for B12 even if folate is low.

Objective: Avoid masking cobalamin deficiency when correcting folate deficiency
ChangedEvidence: Isolated low folate permits folate-directed treatment; improvement of anemia with progression of neurologic signs demands immediate reassessment.

Objective: Differentiate failure to release food-bound B12 from loss of ileal uptake
ChangedEvidence: Reduced gastric acid impedes release from proteins; loss of the terminal ileum impedes uptake of the bound complex.

Objective: Recognize functional cobalamin deficiency despite a misleading blood count or serum level
ChangedEvidence: A normal MCV cannot exclude deficiency in one case; nitrous oxide exposure makes a functional marker particularly informative in the other.

Objective: Use symptoms and the cause of B12 deficiency to guide reassessment after treatment
ChangedEvidence: Early neurologic recovery can lag; progressive symptoms during oral therapy require checking treatment adequacy and alternate diagnoses.

Objective: Trace thiamine-dependent reactions in oxidative and pentose metabolism
ChangedEvidence: A pyruvate challenge tests oxidative decarboxylation; a red-cell transketolase assay tests carbon transfer in the pentose pathway.

Objective: Identify thiamine depletion in nonalcohol-related presentations
ChangedEvidence: Several weeks of vomiting after bariatric surgery confer risk despite a high BMI; prolonged poor intake before refeeding creates risk without surgery.

Objective: Choose the route of thiamine when absorption or urgent neurologic treatment is at issue
ChangedEvidence: Active neurologic illness with unreliable absorption calls for parenteral treatment; later stability allows a maintenance strategy suited to intake.

Objective: Identify vitamin C sources when a restrictive diet lacks produce
ChangedEvidence: The first diet excludes both fresh and fortified sources; the second retains a useful vegetable source despite excluding citrus.

Objective: Recognize a deficiency pattern when routine hemostasis tests are unrevealing
ChangedEvidence: Follicle-centered bleeding and coiled hairs suggest vascular fragility; isolated joint bleeding without these findings warrants another explanation.

Objective: Prevent recurrence after treating vitamin C deficiency when food access changes
ChangedEvidence: Reliable access to tolerated produce permits a food-based maintenance plan; recurring exclusion for sensory reasons calls for an alternative and support.

Objective: Distinguish the circulating marker of vitamin D stores from the active hormone
ChangedEvidence: Substrate depletion can occur with a maintained active hormone; impaired renal activation can occur despite adequate substrate.

Objective: Separate vitamin D excess from PTH-dependent hypercalcemia
ChangedEvidence: A suppressed PTH with large supplement exposure differs from an inappropriately elevated PTH in a second hypercalcemic patient.

Objective: Use product strength and total intake to prevent recurrent vitamin D toxicity
ChangedEvidence: One patient misreads micrograms as IU; a second combines the same active ingredient across two products.

Objective: Account for the water contained in enteral formula
ChangedEvidence: A formula contributes less free water than its full volume; an interruption reduces the amount of that water actually delivered.

Objective: Choose a gastric or postpyloric feeding route using the site of dysfunction
ChangedEvidence: Normal gastric delivery is available in one case; severe upper-GI dysfunction with a usable distal gut changes the route.

Objective: Investigate inadequate enteral delivery before changing formula concentration
ChangedEvidence: Frequent fasting periods reduce actual feeding time; documented full delivery with persistent weight loss requires a different evaluation.

Objective: Trace the intracellular shift in electrolytes during refeeding
ChangedEvidence: An insulin-driven shift lowers circulating phosphate; a normal value before calories does not exclude depleted total-body stores.

Objective: Recognize a high-risk refeeding course from serial measurements
ChangedEvidence: The timing of a phosphate fall after energy delivery supports refeeding, whereas a low value before any calories prompts investigation of preexisting causes.

Objective: Respond to metabolic instability during nutrition support
ChangedEvidence: A clinically important electrolyte fall interrupts planned advancement; stable measurements and tolerance permit cautious progression.

Objective: Explain edema from a leaky alveolar barrier
ChangedEvidence: At similar left atrial pressures, inflammatory barrier injury allows protein-rich fluid into airspaces. Pure hydrostatic edema can occur with intact permeability.

Objective: Assess whether hydrostatic edema explains the acute lung findings
ChangedEvidence: The same bilateral opacities have different explanations when a new valve lesion fully accounts for edema versus when respiratory failure follows sepsis with no sufficient hydrostatic explanation.

Objective: Apply the severe ARDS proning trial to a patient decision
ChangedEvidence: The trial estimated benefit for prolonged sessions in ventilated patients with severe hypoxemia. Its observed absolute benefit cannot be applied directly to brief proning of mildly hypoxemic ambulatory patients.

Objective: Connect intrathoracic pressure to venous return in tension physiology
ChangedEvidence: A large pressure rise narrows the venous return gradient; pressure relief restores the gradient without requiring more circulating blood.

Objective: Interpret the limits of bedside pleural ultrasound
ChangedEvidence: Loss of sliding alone is nonspecific. A transition between sliding and a pneumothorax pattern provides more specific local evidence.

Objective: Counsel on air travel after spontaneous pneumothorax
ChangedEvidence: Residual pleural air precludes ordinary commercial flight. A patient with radiographic resolution can use the recommended waiting interval before flight.

Objective: Explain end-expiratory instability when surfactant is deficient
ChangedEvidence: At a fixed surface tension a smaller airspace requires higher distending pressure; lowering tension can offset the reduced radius.

Objective: Identify the window for antenatal prevention of neonatal RDS
ChangedEvidence: Imminent preterm birth at 29 weeks supports a first antenatal corticosteroid course. Low likelihood of birth within seven days changes the decision.

Objective: Adjust respiratory support after surfactant improves lung mechanics
ChangedEvidence: Rapidly improved oxygenation calls for oxygen titration. Increasing delivered volume at the same set pressure calls for adjustment of ventilator support.

Objective: Explain why conventional pulse oximetry can mislead in methemoglobinemia
ChangedEvidence: A conventional two-wavelength reading may stay near 85% despite changing oxygenation; a multiwavelength co-oximeter measures dyshemoglobin fractions.

Objective: Distinguish failed oxygen transfer from oxidized hemoglobin
ChangedEvidence: Severe hypoxemia from poor alveolar transfer lowers arterial oxygen tension; oxidant injury can produce cyanosis with normal tension and a measurable dyshemoglobin fraction.

Objective: Plan reassessment after an antidotal response to an oxidant
ChangedEvidence: A sustained fall after a short exposure differs from recurrent elevation during prolonged oxidant activity after dapsone.

Objective: Link hypoactive delirium to impaired attention despite quiet behavior
ChangedEvidence: An immobile quiet patient with new inattention still has evidence of delirium. A calm patient accurately sustaining attention with baseline interaction supplies different evidence.

Objective: Identify modifiable contributors when delirium is suspected
ChangedEvidence: New desaturation calls for immediate physiologic assessment; an equipment problem can instead make a hearing-impaired person appear inattentive.

Objective: Interpret evidence for a multicomponent delirium prevention program
ChangedEvidence: An observed risk difference quantifies events across groups; matching without randomization limits attributing all of that difference to the intervention.

Objective: Recognize regional tissue loss and its effect on adjacent CSF spaces
ChangedEvidence: Regional atrophy widens neighboring sulci and CSF spaces. Added lesion volume instead tends to efface nearby spaces.

Objective: Distinguish language-led degenerative syndromes by the failing language function
ChangedEvidence: Loss of word meaning with fluent grammar differs from effortful agrammatic output with relatively preserved single-word comprehension.

Objective: Match practical support in frontotemporal degeneration to the observed disability
ChangedEvidence: Communication loss with preserved swallowing supports an alternative communication system. Choking and weight loss require a swallowing-safety assessment.

Objective: Relate orexin loss to unstable boundaries between wakefulness and REM
ChangedEvidence: REM atonia intruding during wake can produce cataplexy. Absent awareness during a new collapse should prompt alternative explanations.

Objective: Interpret the numerical components of an adequately prepared MSLT
ChangedEvidence: A short mean latency with two sleep-onset REM periods meets the laboratory pattern; the same latency without those REM periods documents sleepiness alone in the stated setting.

Objective: Reassess functional safety when treating daytime sleepiness
ChangedEvidence: Persistent unintended sleep at the wheel requires immediate driving avoidance and reassessment. Improvement in cataplexy alone does not demonstrate improved alertness.

Objective: Distinguish entrained phase delay from a progressively drifting sleep rhythm
ChangedEvidence: A stable late sleep period is delayed but entrained to the day. Successive daily shifts indicate drift relative to a 24-hour schedule.

Objective: Choose a longitudinal measurement for suspected circadian misalignment
ChangedEvidence: Multiple-day sleep and activity records show phase over time. A single quiet interval cannot distinguish sleep from motionless wake.

Objective: Track treatment of a phase disorder using sleep timing and actual sleep opportunity
ChangedEvidence: A stable shift with preserved sleep duration and better function supports progress. Earlier forced waking without earlier sleep shortens sleep instead.

Objective: Distinguish cognitive slowing from a motor or language constraint on cognitive testing
ChangedEvidence: Slow written responses with preserved oral performance implicate a motor constraint. Difficulty sequencing steps across motor and verbal tasks supports a broader executive problem.

Objective: Assess whether loss of independence after stroke is attributable to cognition
ChangedEvidence: A motor limitation can prevent independent performance despite preserved planning. New medication errors despite adequate dexterity can provide evidence of a cognitive functional deficit.

Objective: Separate vascular risk reduction from antithrombotic treatment without an indication
ChangedEvidence: Established atrial fibrillation or previous ischemic stroke can supply an independent antithrombotic indication. Incidental white-matter changes alone do not automatically justify aspirin.

Objective: Distinguish Lewy pathology from hallmark lesions of competing neurodegenerative disorders
ChangedEvidence: An intraneuronal alpha-synuclein inclusion points to Lewy pathology. An extracellular amyloid plaque instead indicates Alzheimer-type pathology that can coexist.

Objective: Investigate changes in hallucinations in a patient with Parkinson disease dementia
ChangedEvidence: Longstanding well-tolerated hallucinations differ from abrupt hallucinations with fever and inattention. The latter requires assessment for superimposed delirium.

Objective: Reconcile Parkinson medicines during admission in a cognitively vulnerable patient
ChangedEvidence: A time-critical dose omitted by routine scheduling should be restored under the individualized plan. Loss of the swallowing route requires urgent specialist planning rather than abrupt cessation.
